correctness.rationale: With 0 weighted +1 and 1 weighted -1, the regular paperfolding recurrence implies S(2m)=S(m)+1_{m odd} and S(2m+1)=S(m)+1_{m even}. These are exactly the recurrences for the number of runs in the standard binary expansion, so Dyck factors are precisely nonnegative return intervals of binary run count. For equal-length binary endpoints, the two numbers at the first 0/1 boundary force each endpoint suffix to have at most one transition; equality then makes their difference 2^d-2^i with 1<=i<d. Different-length endpoints force baseline run count 1 and hence endpoints 2^i-1 and 2^k-1. Conversely those endpoints give canonical Dyck factors. The verifier independently checks all key identities and finite cases.

originality.rationale: The direct 2023 source states the paperfolding length characterization as Conjecture 6.5 and does not provide a proof. The published range includes i=0, which is incompatible with the even length of nonempty Dyck words; the result proves the natural parity-corrected statement i>=1. Focused searches for the conjecture, exact power-difference formulation, paperfolding Dyck factors, and binary-run aliases found no covering proof. Own current and prior records contain paperfolding results and a different Dyck result from the same source, but none classifies paperfolding Dyck lengths.
residual_risks: The printed i=0 endpoint is almost certainly a parity slip, so the theorem is best read as proving the intended parity-corrected conjecture.
An unindexed note or unpublished proof may contain the same short binary-run argument.

value.rationale: The source explicitly singles out the paperfolding length set as a conjecture. The result resolves the substantive even-length version completely with a short structural invariant, rather than by a finite census: it identifies all possible lengths and gives canonical factors at every allowed length. This is a natural complete classification directly adjacent to the source paper’s established automatic-sequence Dyck results.
